newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia woolgrowers back new sales system.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia woolgrowers back new sales system.

text.p: Grower body the Wool Council of Australia (WCA) has welcomed new arrangements for the selldown of wool from Australia's 2.13 million bale stockpile.
WCA president Rod Thirkell-Johnston said in a statement that the issue had now been resolved and common ground established.
The solution was responsive to woolgrowers' need for change and to the international trade's need for certainty, he said.
As reported, Australia's Minister for Primary Industries John Anderson will take to cabinet changes agreed on at Friday's wool industry Roundtable on the release of stockpile wool.
These involve introduction of a minimum quarterly release requirement of 135,000 bales from January 1, 1997 and a minimum quarterly release of 90,000 bales from July 1, 1997.
A maximum quarterly release of 350,000 bales will apply from January 1, 1997.
The end date for completion of stockpile sales and deliveries is December 31, year 2000.
Present arrangements require quarterly sales of 182,000 to 192,000 bales.
